notes.summary: Actual primary finite pullback, full compact quotient regularization, and openness criterion.
notes.detailedSummary: Rees base change uses global finite semilocal B, actual regular Cartier image divisors and support quotient lattices before G331 completions. Full-fibre MAX regularization needs no openness; continuous full-support kernels on every continuous test imply openness. Normal targets require every minimal source component dominating.
notes.text:
Finite maps of actual primary models and full compact quotients

Use the ENTIRE qualified G331 and G345, with their primary-model, all-support and reduction conventions. Write X_R=V_a(R), C_R=C_geom, and D_R=D_geom. The latter consists of ONE actual decreasing C-net, with bottom allowed; no arbitrary-infimum closure is assumed. Finite algebras are GLOBAL semilocal algebras, with all closed centres over m. A localization B_q need not be finite over R.

For a boundary-primary ideal I, there is a graded surjection Rees_R(I) tensor_R B -> Rees_B(IB), degree r sending I^r tensor B onto (IB)^r. Proj makes Bl_IB(B) a closed subscheme of Bl_I(R) tensor B. The latter is finite over Bl_I(R), so the actual source blowup is finite over the target model. On reduced positive-dimensional components, the primary blowup dominates each component and is the identity away from the marked closed centres. On an f-chart its image ideal is (f), with f regular: f is nonzero at every surviving component generic point. Thus the image is an ACTUAL effective Cartier divisor, supported over m, and equals the pullback target image ideal. Zero-dimensional components have empty blowup and no centred boundary. These statements use the complete 01OF 31.33.1--14 at actual reduced primary blowups.

If a contracted source integral curve maps to a point, the pullback bundle has degree zero; otherwise its degree over the source closed residue field is the target degree times the full function-field degree, divided by the closed residue-field degree. This is the proper-FIELD numerical projection of 0BEL, with inseparability retained. Nonnegative degrees therefore pull back. For a semivaluation of support P, evaluate Cartier data in the valued quotient field Frac(B/P), using the invertible bundle's generic trivialization; its restriction uses Frac(R/(P intersect R)). The model map identifies the two lattices before completion. G331's comparison now gives pullback on C and actual D, and its full-fibre descent theorem applies to every reduced finite injection.

For any reduced finite map put A=R/ker(R->B). Its intrinsic boundary is precisely the closed subset v(ker)=infinity of X_R, with the restricted primary gauge, and B->A has continuous surjective compact restriction rho. This is an exact image, not a positive ambient extension. For normalization S, retain every normal closed centre. Fibres are singletons at finite conductor value; at infinite value they are exactly equal restrictions to S/c over R/c. Lower-dimensional centres and nonminimal supports remain.

Here is the topological rule needed below. For a continuous surjection rho:Y->X of compact Hausdorff spaces and ANY bounded-above extended F on X, let F*=inf_{U neighbourhood x} sup_U F. Then
  (F rho)*(y) <= F*(rho y), and F*(x)=MAX_{rho y=x}(F rho)*(y).
The first follows by pulling back neighbourhoods. For the second, take any finite t greater than the fibre maximum. Each fibre point has a neighbourhood where F rho<t; a finite subcover gives an open O containing the fibre. The compact complement has closed image missing x, so some neighbourhood U of x has rho^-1 U contained in O. Hence sup_U F<=t. Let t decrease to the maximum; the same argument for every finite t treats maximum=-infinity. A USC function attains its maximum on a compact fibre. No openness was used. If rho is open, images of neighbourhoods give the reverse pointwise inequality, so (F rho)*=F* rho.

A continuous FULL-support positive kernel implies openness. Given y in an open O, choose continuous h>=0 supported in O with h(y)>0. At x=rho y full support gives T h(x)>0. Continuity on ALL continuous tests makes {T h>0} an open neighbourhood of x contained in rho(O). Applying this at every y proves rho(O) open. Gauge tests alone suffice only after their all-support difference lattice has been proved dense.

For a normal DOMAIN target and a reduced finite source whose EVERY minimal component dominates, sum the G331 norm kernels on all domain components. The kernels are continuous and their union is the FULL fibre; thus rho is open. Normalization of each source component causes no loss, by full lifting. If vertical components occur, this kernel omits their support points and the openness inference is invalid; n5 supplies an exact counterexample.

notes.summary: Reduced-flat determinant kernels and positive full-fibre maxima on C and actual D nets.
notes.detailedSummary: Every Artinian valuation fibre retains inseparable/nilpotent lengths. Coefficient ideals give norm/minimum identities, all-support test density gives choice independence/full support/continuity, and actual primary coefficient truncations preserve the minimum. Normal nonvertical maxima descend via splitting orbits.
notes.text:
Determinant kernels and positive fibre maxima

Let R->B be reduced finite FLAT of rank d>0. Over the local target B is a finite free module. Choose finite R-MODULE generators g_j of an ideal J (possible because B is finite over R). Let C_i(J) be the coefficient ideal of the degree-i characteristic coefficient of multiplication by sum T_j g_j, and N(J)=C_d(J). Changing basis conjugates the multiplication matrix; changing R-module generators gives R-linear substitutions in both directions. Hence coefficient ideals are independent. Determinants are top-exterior-power scalars and commute with arbitrary base change. The actual complete 0BD2 CURRENT 31.18.6 proves the matrix/conjugation and polynomial-base-change formulation; the exterior-power interpretation is the same elementary determinant. If J contains a^r B, redundant generators x in a^r give pure norm coefficients x^d, so N(J) contains a boundary power and is unit-or-primary.

Fix ANY base semivaluation with support P. First pass to K=Frac(R/P). The d-dimensional algebra B tensor K can be nonreduced. Over a finite splitting extension it decomposes into Artinian local factors of lengths l_j with sum l_j=d. On a composition series, multiplication by an element acts by its residue scalar h_j on every quotient; therefore its characteristic polynomial is product(t-h_j)^l_j. The l_j include inseparability and nilpotence, even over a reduced source. Lift the quotient valuation to a finite integral splitting algebra. Gauss coefficient minimum is multiplicative: divide a polynomial by a least-valued coefficient and reduce to a nonzero polynomial over the valuation residue field; products stay nonzero. Polynomials vanishing modulo support have infinite minimum. Applied to the norm family this gives
  v N(J)=sum_j l_j w_j(J).
Boundary-power ideals make these values finite.

The rational ideal-difference span separates ALL support points: (g)+a^N gives min(w(g),N), and centre-separating ideals handle the semilocal pieces. It contains constants and is a lattice, since
 min(vI-vJ,vK-vH)=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH).
Its real uniform closure is all continuous functions by the compact lattice approximation argument in G331. Thus the mass-d measure sum l_j delta_wj is independent of all splitting/lifting choices: its integrals on this dense span are fixed. Any source fibre point can itself be extended to a splitting field of its support quotient and then the same Artinian factorization. It occurs with positive length. Choice independence therefore proves FULL fibre support, at most d atoms, and no omitted supported lift. The coefficient identity proves continuity on ideal tests; density and the fixed mass bound prove it on every continuous test. The trace tau H is positive, continuous-valued, and sends -wJ/q to -vN(J)/q, hence preserves C. A finite positive sum commutes with an actual decreasing nonpositive extended net: directedness handles all finite summands simultaneously, and any bottom summand makes the sum bottom. Consequently tau preserves D using the SAME net, without flattening.

The FULL fibre maximum also preserves these classes. Put m=min_{rho w=v} w(J). Then
  m=min_{1<=i<=d} v C_i(J)/i.
Every root residue has value at least m, so all degree-i coefficients have value at least i m. Choose a generator attaining m at a least-valued fibre point. Its monic characteristic equation cannot have its leading term uniquely least-valued, so some specialized coefficient has value <=i m. Specialization is an R-linear combination of family coefficients, giving the other inequality. The C_i may NOT be primary. Let L=sup_X v C_d(J)/d, finite, and choose an integer N>dL. Replacing EVERY C_i by C_i+a^N changes its value to min(vC_i,N). Since N/i>L>=m, it preserves the displayed minimum EXACTLY. Therefore MAX_fibre(-wJ/q) is a maximum of genuine unit-or-primary rational profiles and belongs to C. The maximum operator is 1-Lipschitz, hence preserves uniform C closure. Finite fibres imply max inf_alpha H_alpha=inf_alpha max H_alpha for a decreasing net, proving actual D preservation.

For a normal target with every source minimal component dominating, take a finite normal splitting field for each component. All extensions of a quotient-support valuation lie in the full orbit of its embeddings: the G331 full-support norm proof supplies this without a defectlessness assertion. The maximum of the finitely many embedding pullbacks is a C or D function invariant on all splitting restriction fibres. G331's positive descent puts its base maximum in C or D. Take the maximum over every component. This proves positive FULL fibre maximum and openness without flatness in precisely the nonvertical normal-target range.

notes.summary: Selected E on all stated USC obstacles, exact positivity/quotient laws and smooth BFJ identification.
notes.detailedSummary: E is positive iff raw has an actual greatest D minorant. Finite continuous obstacles reduce to continuous raw C envelopes. Open positive-MAX maps commute for all obstacles; arbitrary injections have the constrained full-fibre-MAX rule. BFJ identification is only the closed smooth affine algclosed characteristic-zero fixed-dual-complex signature.
notes.text:
The specified geometric envelope, its positive domains, and exact quotient rules

For every bounded-above extended USC obstacle phi on X_R define p_R(phi)=sup{u in D_R:u<=phi} and SELECT E_R(phi)=p_R(phi)*. Bottom is always a competitor; empty boundaries have their unique empty function. Thus p<=E<=min(phi,0), including partial-bottom obstacles. E belongs to D if and only if the raw supremum is an actual greatest D minorant; in that case E=p. Indeed a positive E is itself an admissible competitor, and the converse uses USC of every D function. This defines a selected operator even where positivity fails; it imports no general P12.3 envelope-existence grant.

For finite continuous phi, the raw C and D suprema agree. If u=inf g_alpha<=phi, compactness of the increasing strict-test open cover {g_alpha<phi+epsilon} gives one index valid everywhere. Then g_alpha-epsilon is a C minorant and is >=u-epsilon. Hence p is finite LSC as a supremum of continuous minorants. E is positive iff p is continuous, and then p belongs to C: finite maxima of minorants approximate a continuous p uniformly by compact covers. Conversely continuous p is such a uniform limit, hence E=p in C. For reduced curves G331 gives the full nonpositive branch orthant, so E(phi)=min(phi,0) on every branch, including bottom values.

For the open maps with positive full-fibre MAX of n2, raw envelopes commute for EVERY stated USC obstacle. An upstairs competitor u<=phi rho gives downstairs MAX u<=phi in D, while base competitors pull back. Thus p_B(phi rho)=p_R(phi) rho. Openness and n1's regularization rule give E_B(phi rho)=E_R(phi) rho. By G331 full descent, positivity holds on one side exactly when it holds on the other.

For ANY reduced finite injection constrain upstairs competitors to be constant on EVERY fibre. G331 identifies their raw supremum with p_R(phi) rho. Its ordinary upstairs USC regularization E_con may fail fibre constancy. N1 proves the exact unconditional formula
  E_R(phi)(x)=MAX_{rho y=x} E_con(y).
The base selected envelope is positive iff E_con is in D AND fibre constant. If base E is positive its pullback equals the constrained raw function, so regularization changes nothing. Conversely a positive fibre-constant E_con descends positively and the full-maximum formula identifies that descent with E_R. The unconstrained source envelope E_B(phi rho) is >=E_con, giving only
  E_R(phi)<=MAX_fibre E_B(phi rho).
There is no universal pointwise pullback inequality. If source E_B is positive, equality E_B=E_R rho holds exactly when E_B is fibre constant: positive descent then makes it a base competitor, and the reverse implication is immediate. If both envelopes are positive, base pullback is a source competitor, giving the pointwise inequality in that conditional domain. Noninjective maps use their exact image; n5 disproves ambient extension.

An explicit smooth specialization completes the operator identification, within the EXACT BFJ closed smooth affine, algebraically closed characteristic-zero setting of G331/G345. Let h be a bounded real USC obstacle determined on one BFJ dual complex, h=h r_pi. The published nef envelope W=sup{nef Z<=Z(h)} is well-defined: a sufficiently negative multiple of Z(m) bounds below, finite maxima of competitors form a directed net, and coefficientwise closure of the nef cone contains its finite supremum. G331 identifies its all-retraction function g_W with a bounded D function. At divisorial points g_W<=h. On each simplex g_W is continuous by the granted substantive closed-face theorem; density of rational divisorial points and USC of h extend the inequality there. At every support,
  g_W(v)<=g_W(r_pi v)<=h(r_pi v)=h(v).
Every D minorant of h has nef coefficient divisor <=Z(h), hence <=W, and its all-retraction extension is <=g_W. Thus p=E=g_W. This is precisely the BFJ fixed-dual-complex envelope, not a universal smooth or singular positivity assertion for all USC obstacles. The complete BFJ 3.15--3.22 statements AND proof of 3.18 were freshly read; multiplier/subadditivity history remains disclosed published background at these hypotheses only.

notes.summary: All-field node: selected envelope loses positivity and has reverse gap ONE under normalization.
notes.detailedSummary: The two-plane conductor quotient and exact primary masks determine the raw and USC envelopes. Constrained upstairs regularization is continuous (-1,-2) but not fibre constant; the second shared lift gives gap ONE. Full source schemes include off-diagonal vertical self-base-change components.
notes.text:
All-field two-plane conductor counterexample with exact primary masks

Over ANY field k let R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), a=m, A1=k[x,z]_(x,z), A2=k[y,z]_(y,z), S=A1 times A2. R=A1 fibre-product over T=k[z]_(z) with A2; its conductor is (x,y), R/c=T and S/c=T times T. Each plane is normal. The normalization quotient identifies only w1 killing x and w2 killing y, both giving z value one; all other points remain separate. Let v0 be their common restriction. Thus the example retains nonminimal supports, schemes, and the conductor-infinite stratum.

Take phi=-1-1/v(y), with 1/infinity=0. It is finite continuous. On the first plane it is -1. On the second it is <=-2 at the ordinary m-order o2, with value -2 there. Every negative primary profile u satisfies u(w)<=u(o_i), since w(m)=1 implies w(J)>=ord_m J. This inequality survives uniform and actual decreasing limits. Therefore every second-plane D minorant is <=-2 everywhere. Upstairs the constant tuple (-1,-2) is a C minorant and equals the selected envelope.

For N>=2 put alpha=1/(N-1). On the first plane the ACTUAL PRIMARY mask
 h_N=-(1-alpha)-alpha w((x,z^N))
is <=-1, equals -2 at w1, and has h_N->-1 at each fixed off-shared point. At w1, w(z)=1 and w(x)=infinity, so the mask has value -(1-alpha)-alpha N=-2 exactly. The tuple (h_N,-2) is full-fibre constant, hence descends into C_R by G331, and is <=phi. Consequently the raw base envelope is -1 at all first-plane off-shared points and -2 at all second-plane points, including v0.

Monomial valuations w_M(x)=M,w_M(z)=1 converge on EVERY polynomial and local unit to w1: for large M the least x-degree decides whether the value stabilizes or tends to infinity. The analogous sequence on the other plane converges to w2. The first sequence raises the base USC value at v0 to -1. At second-plane off-shared points a conductor-finite neighbourhood excludes the first branch, so the regularized value remains -2. Thus
 E_R=-1 on the entire first plane INCLUDING v0; E_R=-2 on second-plane off-shared points.
Its pullback is not D: at w2 it is -1 while at o2 it is -2, violating the order inequality. The constrained raw upstairs regularizes to the continuous C tuple (-1,-2), which is NOT fibre constant. At the second shared lift E_R rho=-1>E_S=-2, a reverse-direction gap of exactly ONE. These computations prove failure of positive selected envelopes and failure of universal pointwise pullback<=source-envelope without openness.

The same two sequences show that a continuous full-support generic degree-one trace cannot exist on all continuous tests: for the clopen component test its integral is 1 along the first singleton fibres and 0 along the second singleton fibres, but both approach v0. No assigned value at v0 can make it continuous. Normalization self-base-change retains vertical components:
  (S tensor_R S)_red=A1 times T times T times A2.
The off-diagonal T components map into the shared line. Discarding them would change the full conductor fibres.

notes.summary: Normal exact-image and vertical-injection obstructions, with both envelopes positive.
notes.detailedSummary: For k[[x,y]]/(xy) the intrinsic envelope is (-1,0), while ambient E=-1 and no D extension exists by the normal zero dichotomy. notes.text:
Exact-image localization and the normal-target vertical obstruction

Let R=k[[x,y]], a=(x,y), and Q=R/(xy). The same formulas hold in the localized polynomial ring, and G331's full completion homeomorphism identifies their primary profiles. For phi=-1/v(x), with 1/infinity=0, the ordinary order o gives phi(o)=-1. As in n4 every D_R function satisfies u(v)<=u(o); the constant -1 is a minorant. Hence E_R(phi)=-1. On the intrinsic curve quotient, its two branches have obstacle values (-1,0), and G331's curve cone gives E_Q=(-1,0). The value gap on the y-branch is ONE.

There is no D_R extension of this intrinsic envelope. Such an extension would be zero at a supported point and negative at another; G331's normal-domain zero dichotomy forces a D_R function with any zero value to be identically zero. The primary profiles -v((x^N,y))/N restrict to (-1,-1/N), but their ambient increasing pointwise limit is not USC and is not a permitted decreasing completion. A noninjective trace therefore lives on the EXACT quotient, with its intrinsic dimension and arity.

Now inject R diagonally into B=R times Q by r->(r,r mod xy). This is finite, reduced, and has a vertical minimal component. The source selected envelope is the C tuple (-1,(-1,0)); both source and base selected envelopes are positive, yet they do not commute. A clopen singleton curve branch upstairs maps to a nonopen singleton downstairs: monomial valuations v_M(x)=M,v_M(y)=1 tend to its supported point. Thus the map is nonopen despite the normal target. The dominating-domain trace omits the vertical supported lifts and cannot justify a FULL-support kernel. The full-fibre maximum of this C tuple is zero at that supported base point and -1 elsewhere; it is not continuous and not D by the zero dichotomy. This precisely distinguishes n1's all-minimal-components-dominating hypothesis.

The ambient arity is one: G345 gives mu_R(-1)=delta_o, whereas Q has zero-arity intrinsic measure delta_xbranch+delta_ybranch. Q contributes ZERO to B's ambient degree-two product, while both of its support points remain in the potential and conductor domain. Intrinsic quotient arity cannot be substituted into the ambient product formula.

notes.summary: Full all-pulled product projection, actual supported cycles and multigraded module bridge.
notes.detailedSummary: Proper equal-delta top-component cycles precede Chow/multiplicity; Artinian layers retain all thicknesses and field degrees. Current SH multi-Rees intersection squeeze, rational rays and prime filtration give the complete top-polynomial identity without coefficient ordering; dense moments and prescribed bounded D nets yield all arities.
notes.text:
All-pulled geometric products, actual cycles, and the complete module bridge

Let R be reduced excellent local of dimension n>=1 and p=n-1. For ANY reduced finite map R->B, define the ambient source product mu_B^[R] by summing the intrinsic p-slot products on closed centres of dimension n, multiplied by their FULL closed residue-field degrees over k(m). Lower-dimensional centres contribute zero at this degree, but no point is removed. For each top minimal prime P of R put K_P=Frac(R/P), d_P=dim_KP(B tensor_R K_P), allowing d_P=0 when missed. Let j_P:X_(R/P)->X_R be the closed support inclusion. Then for bounded D inputs
 rho_* mu_B^[R](rho*u_1,...,rho*u_p)
   =sum_{dim R/P=n} d_P (j_P)_* mu_(R/P)(j_P*u_1,...,j_P*u_p).       (A)
For n=1 this includes zero arity. Dimension zero has empty boundary and zero measure, without negative arity.

GEOMETRY PRECEDES IDEALS. On actual simultaneous primary blowups the finite map of n1 pulls back the actual Cartier image divisors. On every integral top source component, its image has equal delta-dimension for delta(P)=dim R/P (02QL), and the map is proper dominant with degree the FULL function-field degree, including inseparability. Apply complete 0AYA 42.26.3 to the supported ACTUAL divisor cycle: pushforward of the pulled-back divisor cycle equals the field degree times the original cycle, BEFORE passing to Chow groups. Successive supported Cartier intersections inherit this projection. On a reduced one-dimensional local ring the cycle of a regular parameter is the sum of its component cycles with generic multiplicity one: embed the ring in its component-domain sum; the finite-length discrepancy has equal multiplication kernel and cokernel, so length of the parameter quotient is additive. This explains the reduced generic weights rather than inventing a nilpotent generic rank.

Supported Cartier intersections retain all thicknesses. Their Euler polynomials are R-length Euler characteristics on Artinian thickenings. Filter by powers of m; every resulting coherent sheaf is on a proper scheme over k(m). Apply 0BEL 33.45.1--13 to EACH field layer, with generic sheaf lengths and full numerical field projections, and sum by Euler additivity. In mixed characteristic the unfiltered thickening is not asserted to be a k(m)-scheme. Equal-dimension proper numerical projection includes the full closed residue-degree conversion. The independent real curve-nef atoms and refinement invariance are G345, not an ideal positivity definition.

The bridge to functions is the ACTUAL fixed-primary, ONE-model bridge in qualified G345. On a given primary model its fixed primary correction c0 times generated section modules forms downstairs primary ideals; on the single refinement Bl_(I c0) the IMAGE ideal equals c0 O(kL). It maps to the associated ideal blowup and yields an actual divisor identity there. Real intersection polynomials of these identities converge to the given real Cartier pairing. Thus (A) first applies to genuine supported geometry and its ideal models. Uniform convergence of arbitrary Cartier FUNCTIONS alone would not imply intersection convergence and is not used.

Here is the complete new algebraic projection bridge. For proper primary labels I_0,...,I_p put P_s=product I_i^s_i and H_M(s)=length_R(M/P_s M). The CURRENT SH 17.4.1 setup and complete 17.4.2--4 give eventual multigraded polynomials of total degree <=dim M and the factorial convention. Rees_R(I_i t_i) is a finitely generated Noetherian multigraded algebra. For an exact sequence 0->M1->M2->M3->0 the graded intersection module sum_s(P_sM2 intersect M1)t^s is a submodule of the finite Rees module for M2, hence has finitely many homogeneous generators. With one componentwise bound c on their degrees,
 P_s M1 subset P_s M2 intersect M1 subset P_(s-c) M1
for all sufficiently large s. This is the multi-ideal Artin--Rees content of the full SH 17.1.6. The quotient exact sequence gives H_M2(s) between H_M1(s-c)+H_M3(s) and H_M1(s)+H_M3(s). Along every positive rational ray, the shift changes only lower degree. Divide by the n-th power of the ray parameter. The top homogeneous forms agree on every such ray and hence as polynomials. This proves additivity of the ENTIRE top form. No coefficient order is inferred from polynomial domination.

A finite module has a finite prime filtration: a nonzero quotient contains an element with maximal annihilator, which is prime, and the resulting strictly increasing submodule chain terminates by Noetherianity. Localizing this filtration at a top minimal P counts exactly length_RP M_P factors R/P. Since R is reduced, R_P=K_P is a field. Therefore
 H_B^top=sum_P d_P H_(R/P)^top, and H_R^top=sum_P H_(R/P)^top.
All lower-dimensional factors have degree<n and vanish at the ambient degree. A finite-length B module decomposes over all closed centres, and
 length_R(B/P_s B)=sum_q [k(q):k(m)] length_Bq(B_q/P_s B_q).
This is a composition-series computation; it does not claim B_q finite over R. Over K_P the reduced localization of B is a product of fields, so d_P is the sum of their full separable/inseparable degrees, with missing components zero.

Complete CURRENT SH 17.4.5--7 were also checked. The literal 17.4.7 unquotiented colon length can be infinite. The valid correction from 17.4.6 is length(0:_(M/(x1,...,x_(d-1))M) x_d), equivalently the colon MODULO the previous-parameter submodule. No regular-sequence hypothesis, false unquotiented colon, or 17.5 polynomial-coefficient shortcut enters this argument. The full current proof of 17.4.4 supplies the same intersection squeeze above; unused labels can be deleted by setting their exponents fixed after stabilization, not by evaluating an eventual polynomial outside its range.

G345's EXACT ideal moment, for one TEST ideal I0 and p input ideals, is
 integral(-v(I0)/q0) d mu(-v(I1)/q1,...,-v(Ip)/qp)
   =-e_R(I0^[1],...,Ip^[1])/(q0...qp).
The coefficient e_R has n=p+1 labels and the stated factorial convention; unit labels have zero positive-arity contribution. The top-form identities prove (A) against every such test profile and their difference lattice. Its all-support uniform density and the known reference mass identify the entire Radon measures. Extend first to C inputs by established uniform continuity, then successively through each bounded D representation by G345's bounded prescribed-limit decreasing-NET continuity, testing against fixed continuous functions. Each slot uses its given actual net; no completion flattening is needed. This proves every arity in (A), including lower-support tests. The normalization case has top degree one and precisely G345's full conductor/closed-residue formula. Curves give the actual measure sum_q [k(q):k(m)] ord_q(a) delta_(ord_q/ord_q(a)); finite field and residue degrees give the full ramification-residue rule.

notes.summary: ONE arbitrary source slot: normal traces and full conductor-admissible projection.
notes.detailedSummary: Splitting orbits retain generic inseparable lengths, d/|G| and ed cancellation. General reduced injections use both normalization base-change injections and every normal centre; full fibre constancy is exact admissibility. Reduced-flat base change is reduced and determinant base change proves automatic full admissibility on all supports.
notes.text:
One arbitrary source slot and full conductor admissibility

Assume n>=2, p=n-1. For a normal target domain A and a finite source domain B, let K subset L have degree d. Choose a finite normal splitting extension M/K containing L, E the finite integral closure of A in M, G=Aut_K(M), and e=[M:L]. The complete embedding factorization, with generic inseparable lengths, gives on EVERY support
  rho_E*(T H)=(d/|G|) sum_{g in G} g* pi*H.                       (B)
Here starred functions mean pullback, pi:X_E->X_B, and T is the G331 unnormalized norm trace. Embeddings of L form a transitive G-orbit; their stabilizer multiplicity and inseparable length give d/|G|. Coincident supported lifts retain multiplicity. G331's kernel choice independence proves (B) on nonminimal supports too. Trace preserves C, and the same finite-sum decreasing net preserves D.

Apply (A) to E/A of degree ed and E/B of degree e. The geometric operator is covariant under each A-automorphism of E: actual primary models and supported Cartier cycles are carried isomorphically; alternatively the exact ideal moments, density and G345 continuities prove the same assertion. All remaining pulled-back inputs are G-invariant. Expanding ONLY ONE slot using (B), the E/A formula multiplies mu_A(TH,u2,...) by ed, while the orbit sum is d times the E product with pi*H. The E/B formula makes the latter de times the pushed B product. Cancel ed>0. Thus
 rho_* mu_B^[A](H,rho*u2,...,rho*up)=mu_A(TH,u2,...,up).          (C)
There is no extra degree. Closed residue weights multiply in each field tower, so both routes agree. For a reduced source, decompose into dominating minimal domain components and sum (C). Vertical components are lower-dimensional for this normal target and contribute zero ambient measure, while remaining in the full potential domain.

At ACTUAL PRIMARY divisorial DVRs this trace also has geometric norm meaning. The finite integral closure in L is torsion-free and free of rank d over the excellent DVR. Degrees, towers, the one-slot limitation, and independent gauges

For arbitrary finite towers, top generic degrees compose with weights: d_P(direct)=sum_{Q over P} [K_Q:K_P] d_Q(next). Full closed residue degrees also multiply. Applying (A) twice therefore gives exactly the direct unnormalized all-pulled formula, without a constant-degree assumption. Normal-domain traces compose by grouping all embeddings in a common normal splitting field; generic inseparable lengths multiply, and G331 choice independence proves equality on EVERY support.

For general conductor traces, a tower identity requires BOTH intermediate full admissibilities: H admissible from the last source to the middle, and its traced middle function admissible to the base. These are essential hypotheses, not inferred from direct admissibility. To verify composition normalize each minimal component. A minimal last-source component contracts to a minimal middle component exactly when it dominates it; for an integral extension incomparability makes this intermediate minimal component unique. On dominating chains, the integral closure of the base domain in the final fraction field is also the integral closure of the finite intermediate domain there: integrality is transitive, and coefficients in the base remain coefficients in the intermediate ring. Thus all normal centres and quotient-support trace diagrams group the same field embeddings. Chains vertical over an intermediate domain do not contribute its normal trace; lower and zero centres remain in both admissibility tests. After the two positive full descents, uniqueness in G331 identifies the composite with the direct trace. Direct fibre constancy alone supplies no intermediate positive descent.

Finite flat kernels compose on every Artinian valuation fibre. Filter a lower local factor by its composition series of length l. The next finite flat algebra tensors this series exactly; after splitting, each upper residue factor of length m_j appears l times. The direct lengths are l m_j. This retains nilpotence and inseparability and agrees with determinant transitivity (also on generic product fields and hence over a reduced base). Constant ranks multiply, so normalized flat averages compose.

For varying branch degrees normalized composition fails sharply over ANY field. Let A=k[[t]], B=A times A, F=A times k[[s]], with t=s^2 in the second branch. Laurent parity gives field degree two in every characteristic. On normalized links take H=(0,-1). The direct weighted average is -2/3; successive normalized averages give -1/2. Both unnormalized traces are -2. Comparing each branch coefficient proves that normalized averages compose exactly when the next generic degree is constant over each intermediate fibre. In characteristic two the same example retains the purely inseparable degree.

More than ONE arbitrary source slot is false even for flat maps. Take a three-dimensional regular R with a=m, B=R times R, H=(-1,0), V=(0,-1). The source mixed product is zero because each component has a zero input. Both traces are -1, so the target mixed product has reference mass e(m)=1; both normalized traces are -1/2, giving mass 1/4. This exact contradiction prevents any all-arbitrary-slots trace formula. Only (C)--(D) are claimed.

For base primary b let t(v)=v_a(b)>0 and G(v)=v/t(v). G331 changes every potential and obstacle by division by t; multiplication/division by a positive continuous factor commutes with USC regularization, including partial bottom (local two-sided bounds on the factor give the extended inequalities). Thus E_b(phi_b)(Gv)=E_a(phi_a)(v)/t(v), and positive domains correspond. G345 gives EXACTLY ONE measure factor:
 mu_b(u_b)=G_*[t mu_a(u_a)].
This is raw reference mass, not probability normalization.

If the source uses an INDEPENDENT primary gauge c, for w in V_c(B) put lambda(w)=w(aB) and s(w)=w/lambda(w). Then H_c(w)=lambda(w) H_(aB)(s(w)). Convert H_c/lambda BEFORE applying any trace. Pulled-back target inputs in this gauge are lambda(w) u(rho_c w). The exact source law is
 mu_(aB)=s_*[lambda mu_c]
